name: The Three-Point Architecture Frame
description: Complex systems—whether industrial, mechanical, or computational—frequently suffer from cascade failures, structural fragmentation, and premature systemic death due to rigid, "tightly coupled" component designs. To address these universal vulnerabilities, this article establishes a cross-disciplinary standard for engineering diagnostics: The Three-Point Architecture Frame. Grounded in the absolute mathematical foundations of relational algebra, category theory, and cybernetics, this frame serves as an unassailable System Benchmark for general reliability and failure prevention. Conformance to this benchmark is evaluated through a universal, two-tier diagnostic mechanism: the Dual-Question Screening Protocol, which functions as the active Test Protocol. By validating that a system satisfies the structural prerequisites of segregation and lifecycle continuity, this framework ensures that the critical core of any architecture remains permanently active, resilient, and operational. Beyond physical engineering, this reliability diagnostic doubles as a rigorous risk-assessment baseline for institutional asset allocation, directly linking systemic uptime to long-term asset security.
